subject.title: [Bug 6.1] Silent config auto-patch from memory-core + error-message auto-fix breaks all cron jobs on hosts without Docker

question: Should host-exec-capable agents or plugin cron jobs ever be allowed to invoke `openclaw config patch`, and where should OpenClaw enforce that boundary?
rationale: The remaining issue crosses persisted config writes, agent-visible sandbox guidance, host exec authority, and plugin-owned cron behavior; source inspection supports the risk but not a single safe mechanical fix.

options.title: Block non-operator config writes
options.body: Require explicit operator provenance or approval for CLI config mutations initiated from agent/cron exec and remove protected config-write instructions from assistant-visible runtime errors.

options.title: Only harden error wording
options.body: Remove config assignments from assistant-visible sandbox errors while leaving CLI config patch authority unchanged.

options.title: Defer for a maintainer reproduction
options.body: Wait for concrete logs or a maintainer reproduction of the auto-writer before changing config mutation semantics.

recommendation.title: Block non-operator config writes
recommendation.body: Require explicit operator provenance or approval for CLI config mutations initiated from agent/cron exec and remove protected config-write instructions from assistant-visible runtime errors.

likelyOwner.reason: The broadest feature-history trail across config, security, sandbox, and memory-core surfaces points to this person as the best routing candidate for the boundary decision.
